assessment.evidence: INT-D-007 confirms GDPR, conditional SFDR, conditional AIFMD and EU AI Act boundaries; INT-D-009 confirms only the conditional DORA trigger and interim evidence boundary. Coverage revision 002 maps 25 obligation clusters to requirements. Official-source, date and article-level mappings remain explicit accountable-owner work.

Requirements Markdown lines 113-117 and catalogue SR-009 require DORA-aligned evidence pending General Counsel's entity record and expressly prohibit a formal DORA compliance claim. VAL-001 keeps applicability or exemption and resulting obligations open.

SR-001, SR-002 and SR-007 cover location, transfers and privileged access, but no active requirement translates INT-D-002's confirmed EU/member-state legal-governance and foreign-jurisdiction-exposure outcome.

DR-002 through DR-006 and SR-002/SR-003 cover licensing, minimisation, special-category exclusion, provenance, retention, legal holds, working-copy deletion, transfer governance and no foundation-model training. Exact source schedules and detailed privacy evidence remain owned validation work.

DR-001 records source domains and owners and TR-001 isolates production-confidential data, but the catalogue does not record INT-D-003's confirmed highly-confidential classification or require classification-bound handling.

FR-002, AR-001, AR-002, SR-006, NR-001 and NR-002 define assistive use, human and specialist review, retained decision authority, prohibited actions, citations, unsupported-claim thresholds, risk detection, logging and auditable review.
SR-008 assigns the verdict to Internal Audit and prevents Model Risk from issuing it, matching INT-D-009.

All 29 active requirements have stable acceptance IDs, preconditions, actions, observable outcomes, thresholds, environments and evidence sources. VAL-002 through VAL-005 visibly retain definitions and evidence details required before execution.
The candidate claims no architecture, Azure service, deployment, runtime result, AI risk classification, formal DORA compliance, certification, attestation or Phase 1 approval.

findings.title: Confirmed confidentiality and legal-jurisdiction sovereignty outcomes are not fully translated into active requirements
basis: INT-D-003 confirms deal, financial, legal and portfolio data as highly confidential.

INT-D-002 confirms that contracts, data processing, incident handling and dispute governance remain subject to applicable EU/member-state law and that foreign-jurisdiction exposure is explicitly assessed and accepted.

The 29-requirement catalogue has source ownership and environment isolation, but no active requirement records the highly-confidential classification with classification-bound handling and no requirement covers the confirmed legal-governance/foreign-exposure outcome.
findings.impact: Phase 2 and Phase 3 could design controls without a complete handling boundary for highly confidential data or an acceptance gate for foreign-jurisdiction exposure, despite both outcomes being human-confirmed.
findings.remediationProposal: Append active, sourced and testable requirement coverage for the confirmed highly-confidential classification and its handling outcomes, and for EU/member-state legal governance plus explicit assessment and accountable acceptance of foreign-jurisdiction exposure. Obtain General Counsel, CISO and data-owner confirmation of wording and acceptance evidence; regenerate Markdown, HTML, catalogue, manifest and independent receipt.
findings.reReviewRequirement: Material remediation invalidates this hash-bound review. Re-review the complete revised scope by AFF-A and AFF-B against the same new unchanged manifest.

verdictRationale: The candidate correctly bounds GDPR, SFDR, AIFMD, EU AI Act and conditional DORA; it preserves privacy, privileged-access, AI-safety, human-oversight, audit, independent-validation and phase boundaries and makes no formal DORA compliance claim. However, one unresolved major traceability defect omits two confirmed security and sovereignty outcomes from the active requirements baseline. A conforming verdict is not available until the complete revised scope is re-reviewed.
nextAction: AFF-1 should consider the owner-facing remediation proposal. Any accepted material change requires a new canonical manifest and complete AFF-A and AFF-B re-review. Do not present this record as approval or compliance certification.
